verdict: NEGATIVE. Correct, gated, and slower. NOT promoted; flag remains off by default.
correctness: Passed every gate it was given: default_path_never_enables_expert_wave_without_flag, device_silu_mul_v21_against_f64_over_several_vectors under Parity V2.1, and the static drain check. Default resident path re-verified 3/3 after merge. The implementation is not wrong; it is slower.
static_expectation_vs_outcome: Drains were expected to fall 234 -> 78 per token and full resident waits 583 -> 430. Fewer synchronizations did NOT produce a faster token -- it produced a 71 percent slower one.
what_this_falsifies: The assumption that synchronization count is the thing to minimize. The post-memoization ledger already put metal_synchronize_cpu_wait at 520.3 ms of 2,339 ms and 0.83 ms per synchronization; removing two thirds of the drains should have bought at most a few hundred ms, and instead cost 585 ms. Collapsing three batched matvec calls into one fused wave evidently serializes work the three-call path was overlapping, or the fused kernel is materially less efficient per expert than the batched matvec it replaced.
controller_note: This is the second time a structurally appealing collapse has failed to pay. GPU-resident state was exactly 1.00x; expert-wave is 0.59x. Both were necessary-sounding and neither moved the number. The measured ledger has now outranked architectural reasoning three times tonight -- syncs at 23 percent not 100, lm_head as the real prize, and now fewer drains being actively worse.
next: Do not pursue further drain reduction on the assumption it pays. Profile the expert-wave path itself to find where the 585 ms went before attempting <=8 or <=3 drains. If fused waves are inherently slower per expert here, the collapse ladder below 78 is not the route to TG20 and the remaining levers are active-expert reduction, KV/state reduction, and sequential-depth collapse.
